College Visit Marketing Plan — Prakrit AI
Objective
Drive student signups for Prakrit AI across college visits spanning IT, Medical, and MBA institutions. Students manage their own health and their family’s — Prakrit AI solves that for them.

What We’re Pitching
Prakrit AI
A family health management and AI-powered health companion platform. Upload medical reports, track medications, get 24/7 AI health assistance — all in one place, for the whole family.

Primary audience: Students across all streams
CTA: Join the waitlist / Sign up free
Waitlist URL: prakrit.ai/join-waitlist
Live proof: 20,000+ users, 75%+ weekly repeat rate in 3 Months


Why Students? The Core Insight
Most college students are:

Living away from home for the first time
Managing their own health independently (possibly for the first time)
Responsible for keeping track of family health back home
Confused by lab reports and prescriptions
Not going to a doctor until something is seriously wrong

Prakrit AI is exactly what they need — and most of them don’t know it exists yet.

College Segmentation & Pitch Angle
IT / Engineering Colleges





























AngleDetailHook”You’re building the future of tech — but who’s managing your health? Prakrit AI uses the same AI stack you study, applied to something that actually affects you every day.”Pain PointTech students ignore health, don’t understand medical reports, have parents calling with health questions they can’t answerResonanceThey’ll appreciate the tech (Claude, OpenAI, Supabase, React) — mention PrakritGPT as a technically impressive AI productCTA”Sign up, upload your last blood test, and see what AI tells you in plain English.”Best TouchpointsCSE/IT dept, coding clubs, tech fests, hostel notice boards
Medical Colleges





























AngleDetailHook”You’re training to explain medical reports to patients — Prakrit AI already does that with AI. Use it for your own family, and understand what the future of patient engagement looks like.”Pain PointMed students’ families constantly send them reports asking “what does this mean?” — Prakrit AI handles that automaticallyResonanceThey understand the clinical value immediately. AI document analysis, health timelines, medication tracking, abnormal value detection — this is their worldCTA”Upload a report right now and watch PrakritGPT explain it the way you’d explain it to a patient.”Best TouchpointsMBBS/BDS/Nursing batches, intern groups, student union, faculty referrals
MBA Colleges





























AngleDetailHook”Health is the one thing you can’t outsource. Prakrit AI gives you and your family a personal health manager — so you can focus on everything else.”Pain PointMBA students are high-pressure, often neglect health, and come from families who need health coordinationResonanceShow the business angle too — 20K users, strong retention, India-first healthtech with LATAM expansion. They’ll appreciate the startup storyCTA”Join the waitlist — it’s free. Try it for your family this week.”Best TouchpointsPlacement cell events, entrepreneurship cells, health & wellness clubs, peer networks

On-Ground Execution Flow
Before the Visit

 Identify college point of contact (student coordinator / placement officer)
 Prepare a 2–3 min live demo: show by demo login → show PrakritGPT explanation

At the Visit (15–20 min) - Demo

Hook (2 min) — “When was the last time you actually understood a medical report? Or helped your parents understand one?”
Problem framing (3 min) — Scattered records, confusing reports, no health continuity between doctor visits
Demo (7 min) — Live: upload a report → PrakritGPT explains it in plain language. Show family profiles, medication tracking, WhatsApp assistant
Social proof (1 min) — 20,000 users, 75%+ come back every week, PrakritGPT launched 2 weeks ago with overwhelmingly positive response
CTA (2 min) — Scan the QR, sign up right now, it’s free
Q&A + collect contacts

After the Visit

 Follow up with the college contact within 24 hours (WhatsApp message with signup link)
 Send a short message to interested students who didn’t sign up on the spot
 Log the visit: college, date, stream, signups collected, follow-up status


Signup Funnel
Student hears pitch / sees demo
          ↓
Scans QR / visits link
          ↓
Joins waitlist or signs up on Prakrit AI
          ↓
Onboarded → uploads first document or sets up family profile


Keep signup frictionless — name, email, phone is enough
Use college-specific QR codes or referral codes to measure which visits convert


Demo Script (Quick Reference)

“Let me show you something. Here’s a real blood test report. I’ll upload it to Prakrit AI right now.”
(Upload → PrakritGPT generates a plain-language explanation)
“That’s what your doctor would take 10 minutes to explain — Prakrit AI does it in seconds. And it flags anything abnormal. You can do this for yourself, your parents, your grandparents.”

For Medical students — add:

“This is what patient engagement looks like in 2026. Your patients will use tools like this between visits.”


Collateral Checklist

 Prakrit AI one-pager (print + digital) — with QR code to signup
 Sample medical report (for live demo — anonymised)
 Short demo logins
 Business card / contact card with WhatsApp number
 Visit tracking sheet (college, date, stream, signups, follow-up)


Messaging Per Audience (Quick Reference)

























AudienceOne-linerEngineering students”Built on AI. Designed for your family’s health. Try it today.”Medical students”This is what your patients will use. You should know it first.”MBA students”Your family’s health, managed like a portfolio — one platform, always updated.”General students”Stop guessing what that report means. Ask Prakrit AI.”

Tracking & Reporting
After each visit, log:

College name & type (IT / Medical / MBA)
Date of visit
Approx. students reached
Signups / waitlist joins collected
Quality leads (students who asked questions / wanted follow-up)
Follow-up status (done / pending)

Prakrit26 — Prakrit AI (Complete Reference)

Family health management and AI-powered health companion platform targeting Indian families. Two folders make up this product: the active codebase (svasthai) and the strategy/documentation archive (PrakritAI).


Product Overview
What it is: A central platform for families to manage health records, analyze medical documents with AI, track medications, and get 24/7 health assistance — all in one place.
Problem it solves: Scattered health records, inability to understand medical reports, medication non-compliance, and lack of continuous health engagement between doctor visits.
Target users: Families, caregivers, individuals managing chronic conditions, anyone confused by medical reports.
Market: India-first (English + Hindi), with LATAM expansion planned.
Stage: Pre-launch / Beta with waitlist (as of April 2026).

Core Features

Family Health Profiles — Separate health records for each family member (spouse, parents, children)
AI Document Analysis — Upload lab reports, prescriptions, X-rays, ultrasounds; get plain-language AI explanations
Medication Tracking — Track medications for all family members, reminders, adherence monitoring
24/7 AI Health Assistant — Context-aware conversational AI with voice mode
PrakritGPT — Advanced document-aware AI chat for deeper health questions
Health Timeline — Chronological record of all documents, consultations, and medications
Health Insights — Cross-report analysis, trend detection, pattern recognition
Emergency Health Card — Store blood type, allergies, emergency contacts, critical medications
WhatsApp Integration — AI health assistant via WhatsApp (Twilio, short-form 8-line responses)
Admin Dashboard — Waitlist management and admin features

Consulting Proposal — Clean Electric
People Architecture for a Hypergrowth EV Battery Company

Intelligence Brief — Who Is Clean Electric?
Clean Electric (Pune, founded 2020) is one of India’s most technically differentiated EV battery startups. Built by three IIT graduates — Akash Gupta (CEO), Abhinav Roy (CTO), and Ankit Joshi (CPO) — the company has developed a patented immersion cooling technology (0Kelvin™) that enables sub-15-minute EV charging, a first in India at mass market price points.
Where they are today:

Backed by institutional investors including Kalaari Capital, Info Edge Ventures, Pi Ventures, and Lok Capital — Seed round (2022) followed by Series A (August 2024)
6,000+ batteries deployed across 100+ locations, 20M+ km covered
12+ active OEM customers including Bounce Infinity and Omega Seiki Mobility
Significant manufacturing capacity scale-up underway post Series A
4 patents granted (India + US) on immersion cooling architecture

Their ambition (stated publicly): “Build a hardware-centric global tech company from India.” — Akash Gupta, Forbes India Podcast

The Real Situation
Clean Electric has built something genuinely impressive: patented technology, institutional backing, real OEM deployments, and strong revenue momentum. They are not a slide-deck startup.
But they are at the most dangerous stage for a hardware company — post-Series A hypergrowth — where product and funding have outpaced the organization’s ability to execute at scale.
The signals are clear:





































SignalWhat It MeansRapid headcount growth post Series AProcesses, culture, and management are all under strainNo visible HR functionA fast-growing team with no People Ops is a ticking clockThree co-founders running engineering, product, and operations simultaneouslyFounder bottleneck — no management layer between them and the teamSignificant manufacturing scale-up plannedIndustrial workforce management, quality systems, and production leadership are all stress-tested at onceHiring only experienced engineers (5–10 years)Premium talent requires premium people practices to retainCGO Sachin Singh recently hiredSignals a pivot to institutional OEM sales — needs a team and a process behind himNo blog content, minimal social presenceZero employer brand investment — a liability when competing for top engineering talent
This is where Perfect Skills comes in.

Proposed Engagement — Six Workstreams
The following is an integrated consulting engagement tailored to Clean Electric’s current stage, team profile, and growth ambitions. It goes well beyond a standard training program.

Workstream 1 — Performance Management Foundation
What: KPI & Goal Setting Framework across all functions
Who: Engineering leads, Manufacturing leads, Software team, Sales/BD
Format: 2-Day Facilitated Workshop + Framework Document
Clean Electric’s three founders are running engineering, product, and operations simultaneously. There is almost certainly no standardized KPI framework — goals are set informally, performance is assessed subjectively, and high performers have no structured path to recognition.
Deliverables:

KPI Design Reference Sheet tailored to EV battery manufacturing (cycle yield, deployment SLA, BMS uptime, OEM satisfaction scores, software release cadence)
SMART Goal Writing with Clean Electric-specific examples
OKR cascade methodology — from company targets down to team-level KPIs
Goal Review Rhythm Guide (weekly standups, monthly reviews, quarterly OKR check-ins)
KPI Maturity Checklist for self-assessment per team

Why now: With 12+ OEM customers and aggressive growth targets, every team needs to know exactly what they’re responsible for delivering — and how it connects to the company’s growth.

Workstream 2 — Organizational Design & Management Layer
What: Org structure design + role architecture for the next phase of growth
Who: Founders + HR (if exists) + functional heads
Format: Consulting Engagement
Clean Electric has three brilliant founders and a growing team — but no visible management layer in between. This is a structural bottleneck that will slow decision-making, create founder burnout, and limit the company’s ability to scale.
Deliverables:

Current org structure mapping and gap analysis
Recommended org design suited to an engineering and manufacturing company at this scale
Role definitions for critical mid-management positions (Engineering Manager, Manufacturing Operations Lead, BMS Software Lead, Sales Operations Manager)
Accountability framework — who owns what, at what level
Delegation matrix — what founders should own vs. hand off
RACI charts for cross-functional processes (OEM onboarding, product launch, quality escalation)

Why now: Post-Series A is exactly when founder-led structures break down. Building a management layer now is far easier than doing it under pressure later.

Workstream 3 — People Function Setup
What: Build the HR/People Operations function from scratch
Who: Founding team + any HR hire they bring in
Format: Consulting + Implementation Support
Clean Electric has no visible HR function despite being a rapidly growing team. This means onboarding is ad hoc, policies don’t exist, and the burden falls on founders and team leads.
Deliverables:

HR Policies & Employee Handbook (joining, leave, code of conduct, performance, exit)
Onboarding & Induction Program — structured 30/60/90-day plan for new hires
HR SOP Library — hiring process, offer letters, appraisal cycle, resignation handling
HR Calendar — annual rhythm of performance reviews, increment cycles, engagement touchpoints
Tools & Systems Recommendations — HRMS setup guidance (Keka, Zoho People, or equivalent)
Job Description Library — standardized JDs for all current and planned roles

Why now: Every week without these systems means inconsistent experiences for new hires, founder time wasted on admin, and growing compliance risk.

Workstream 4 — Compensation & Career Architecture
What: Pay band structure + designation framework + career ladders
Who: Founders + HR
Format: Consulting Document + Reference Framework
Clean Electric is actively hiring experienced professionals in a competitive Pune market for hardware, manufacturing, and software talent. Without structured compensation bands and career ladders, they will lose offers to established players — all of whom have structured HR practices.
Deliverables:

Pay Band Design — market-benchmarked salary ranges across all levels and functions (R&D, Manufacturing, Software/BMS, Sales, Operations, Product)
Designation Rationalization — clean hierarchy from Associate → Senior → Lead → Manager → Senior Manager → Director
Career Ladder — transparent growth paths within each function (Engineering Track, Manufacturing Track, Software Track, Business Track)
Variable Pay & Incentive Guidelines — linking performance ratings to increments and bonuses
Joining Offer Benchmarks — competitive ranges for the experienced profiles they’re actively hiring
EV Sector Benchmarking — compensation positioned against relevant players in the EV and cleantech space

Why now: They’re in active hiring mode for senior profiles. Every unstructured compensation conversation is a risk.

Workstream 5 — Leadership Development for Founders & Emerging Managers
What: Structured leadership capability building for the founding team and first management layer
Who: Co-Founders + emerging team leads
Format: Monthly Coaching Sessions + Workshop
The three co-founders are first-time leaders at scale. They are strong engineers and entrepreneurs — but leading at scale requires a different set of skills: delegation, giving feedback, managing managers, cross-functional alignment, and building culture deliberately.
Deliverables:

Founder Leadership Assessment — strengths, blind spots, working styles
Leadership Workshop — Moving from “doing” to “leading”: delegation, accountability, feedback culture
First-Time Manager Program — for team leads being elevated to management roles (how to run 1:1s, set goals, handle underperformance, build team culture)
Monthly Coaching Cadence — structured sessions with the founding team to embed frameworks and work through real challenges
Decision-Making Framework — what decisions founders make vs. delegate vs. involve the team in

Why now: With Sachin Singh’s hiring, Clean Electric is adding seasoned industry veterans to the team. Managing experienced professionals requires founders to step up as leaders — not just as engineers.

Workstream 6 — Sales Team Capability & OEM Account Management
What: Sales process design + capability building for the commercial team
Who: CGO + sales/BD team
Format: Workshop + Process Documentation
Moving from founder-led sales to a scalable OEM sales engine is Clean Electric’s most critical commercial challenge. Sachin Singh’s hiring as CGO is the right move — but he needs a team, a process, and a playbook behind him.
Deliverables:

OEM Sales Process Design — from lead qualification to technical demonstration to pilot to commercial contract
Sales Capability Workshop — B2B enterprise selling, OEM account management, technical selling (for engineers who interface with OEM teams)
Account Management Framework — how to grow existing OEM relationships from single product to full fleet partnerships
Sales KPI Framework — pipeline metrics, conversion rates, OEM satisfaction scores, revenue per account
Proposal & Presentation Skills — structured training for the team on pitching to OEM procurement and leadership teams
CRM Adoption Support — guidance on implementing a CRM and building pipeline discipline

Why now: Clean Electric’s growth depends entirely on OEM relationships. A structured sales process will close deals faster and at higher contract values.

Why Clean Electric Needs This Now
The post-Series A phase is the most critical — and most fragile — moment for a hardware startup. Here is what happens when people systems don’t keep up with growth:

Top engineers leave because there’s no career path or compensation clarity
OEM deals close slower because the sales team has no process
Manufacturing quality suffers because production teams have no structured KPIs or accountability
Founders burn out because there’s no management layer to absorb decisions
New hires onboard poorly and take months to become productive
Culture becomes accidental rather than intentional — and accidental culture at scale is usually a problem

Neuron Energy, Clean Electric’s closest Pune-based competitor, is aggressively scaling manufacturing capacity. Clean Electric’s differentiation window on technology is real but finite. The companies that win at this stage are the ones that execute faster — and execution speed is a people and systems problem.
